newsitem.title: INDIA: India exempts state shares from capital gains tax.
newsitem.headline: India exempts state shares from capital gains tax.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma has issued a ordinance allowing investment in shares issued by public companies to be exempt from long-term capital gains tax, the government said on Wednesday.
The government said in a statement that Sharma issued the Income Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance on Tuesday, changing certain sections of the Income Tax Act of 1961.

It said that with effect from October 1, 1996, "section 54EA of the Income Tax Act has been amended to include shares issued by public companies (subject to guidelines) along with other assets already specified in the section".
The statement said "investment in such shares would qualify for exemption from long-term capital gains".
It said the ordinance also amended section 80G of the Income Tax Act to extend a 100 percent deduction from taxable income to donations to the National Illness Assistance Fund.
"Donations made to the fund in the financial year 1996/97 (April-March) will be eligible for deduction," the government said.
The ordinance also strengthened provisions to curb tax evasion, it said.
